title: Invariant affine charts for a split torus on a normal ample scheme over an affine base
statement: Let $S$ be an affine Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $X\to S$ be a separated finite-type morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], assume every local ring of $X$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and assume $X$ has an ample invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Let the split torus $T=\mathbf G_{m,S}^r$, for an integer $r\geq0$ [def-sc-gm-ga], act on $X$ over $S$. This means a morphism $a:T\times_SX\to X$ satisfying the unit and associativity identities [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then every point of $X$ has an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq X$ invariant under $T$: $a$ restricts to $T\times_SU\to U$. Thus $X$ admits a covering by $T$-invariant affine open subschemes. The acting torus is required to be split; no assertion for nonsplit tori is included.

source.place: Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.4(3), printed p.32, Adv. Math.65 (1987), followed by weight-homogeneous affine projective charts avoiding the invariant boundary. WANTED local copy; the affine-chart consequence is the supporting lemma stated here.

proof.text: Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$; the ring $A$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], applied to the affine open $S$ of the locally Noetherian scheme $S$. Choose an ample invertible module $L$ as in the hypothesis. By [lem-weil-pbc-ample-very-ample-immersion-affine-base], $X\to S$ admits an immersion into finite-dimensional projective space, so it is quasi-projective in the sense required by [lem-sfb-relative-torus-diagonal-projective-embedding]. Apply that node to the given normal finite-type separated $X$ and split torus $T$; obtain an equivariant immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf P^n_A$ with coordinate weights $w_i$. Normal local domains are reduced (a nilpotent element in a domain is zero). Hence the image $W=j(X)$ is reduced. The empty $X$ case is vacuous; henceforth fix any $x\in X$ and put $p=j(x)$.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space; Tag 01M4, lemma-standard-open. Agent boundary-avoiding weight-chart argument after Thomason Corollary 3.4(3), printed p.32 (local copy WANTED).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-diagonal-projective-boundary] to the invariant reduced locally closed image $W$. It gives invariant reduced closed subschemes $Z,B\subseteq P$, with $W=Z\setminus|B|$, and weight-stability of each boundary equation module $I(B)_d$. By [lem-sfb-projective-closed-subscheme-homogeneous-ideal], the total-degree homogeneous ideal $I=\bigoplus_dI(B)_d$ satisfies $B=\operatorname{Proj}(R/I)$ for $R=A[z_0,\ldots,z_n]$. These are equations on schemes over $A$, not equations inferred from rational points of the fibres.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space; Tag 01M4, lemma-standard-open. Agent boundary-avoiding weight-chart argument after Thomason Corollary 3.4(3), printed p.32 (local copy WANTED).

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p$ be the homogeneous prime of $R$ corresponding to $p$. Since $p\notin|B|=V_+(I)$, choose a total-degree homogeneous $f\in I_d\setminus\mathfrak p$ [def-pc-proj]. Indeed, if every total-degree component of every element of $I$ were in the prime, then $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$. If $d=0$, choose $z_i\notin\mathfrak p$ (the prime does not contain the irrelevant ideal), and replace $f$ by $fz_i\in I_1\setminus\mathfrak p$. Thus $d>0$. Write $f=\sum_mf_m$ by grouping its finitely many monomials by weight. The boundary lemma makes every $f_m$ a member of $I(B)_d$. At least one $h=f_m$ is outside $\mathfrak p$, since otherwise their sum would be in that ideal. Thus $h$ is a positive-total-degree boundary equation with coaction $h\mapsto t^mh$.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space; Tag 01M4, lemma-standard-open. Agent boundary-avoiding weight-chart argument after Thomason Corollary 3.4(3), printed p.32 (local copy WANTED).

proof.text: Put $U=j^{-1}D_+(h)$. It contains $x$. Since $h\in I(B)$, $D_+(h)$ misses $|B|$. The equality $W=Z\setminus|B|$ of Step 2 therefore identifies $U$ with $Z\cap D_+(h)$ as an open subscheme of $Z$. By [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open], $D_+(h)$ is affine because $d>0$. The affine characterization of closed immersions in [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes its intersection with the closed subscheme $Z$ a spectrum of a quotient ring, hence affine. This is where avoidance of the entire boundary is needed.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space; Tag 01M4, lemma-standard-open. Agent boundary-avoiding weight-chart argument after Thomason Corollary 3.4(3), printed p.32 (local copy WANTED).

proof.text: For any $A$-algebra $C$, any $t\in T(C)$ and any $C$-point of $P$, locally represent its homogeneous coordinates in a trivialization of its invertible quotient by $v_0,\ldots,v_n$. The coordinate action replaces $v_i$ by $t^{w_i}v_i$; every monomial of $h$ has weight $m$, so $h(t^{w_0}v_0,\ldots,t^{w_n}v_n)=t^mh(v_0,\ldots,v_n)$. The Laurent monomial $t^m$ is a unit. Consequently the action preserves the open where $h$ generates the corresponding tensor-power line. This local criterion is independent of its frame and applies to nonreduced $C$ too. Apply it to the universal point of $T\times_SU$ and use equivariance of $j$; the action maps into $U$. The open-immersion factorization property [def-weil-open-immersion] gives the restricted action morphism. Its unit and associativity laws follow by composing with the monic inclusion $U\hookrightarrow X$. Since $x$ was arbitrary these opens cover $X$. For $r=0$ the unique weight is zero and the same calculation applies.
